Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html`.

- RIGHT column: "Controls" panel and "Debugger" panel.
  Controls panel: buttons Run, Pause, Step, Reset (ids btn-run, btn-pause, btn-step, btn-reset); a range slider id="speed" min=1 max=200 value=10 with a label showing current value "N instructions/frame"; a file input id="rom-input" (accept any file) with label "Load ROM from file"; a status line id="status" showing RUNNING/PAUSED and loaded ROM name/size.

- Below main row: a short help section explaining: WASD moves the sprite in the built-in demo; full keyboard mapping; that a ROM file can be loaded.

=== EMULATOR CORE (JS class Chip8) ===
- memory: Uint8Array(4096). Font set (16 chars x 5 bytes) loaded at 0x050. Use exactly these 80 bytes: F0 90 90 90 F0, 20 60 20 20 70, F0 10 F0 80 F0, F0 10 F0 10 F0, 90 90 F0 10 10, F0 80 F0 10 F0, F0 80 F0 90 F0, F0 10 20 40 40, F0 90 F0 90 F0, F0 90 F0 10 F0, F0 90 F0 90 90, E0 90 E0 90 E0, F0 80 80 80 F0, E0 90 90 90 E0, F0 80 F0 80 F0, F0 80 F0 80 80 (for digits 0..F in order).
- v: Uint8Array(16) registers V0..VF; I (16-bit); pc starts 0x200; stack: array of 16-bit return addresses; delayTimer, soundTimer; display: Uint8Array(64*32); keys: Uint8Array(16); drawFlag.
- reset(): clear memory, reload font at 0x050, clear registers/I/stack/timers/display/keys, pc=0x200.
- loadRom(Uint8Array): copies bytes at 0x200 (max 0xFFF-0x200), pc=0x200.
- cycle(): fetch opcode = memory[pc]<<8 | memory[pc+1]; pc += 2; decode & execute ALL 35 opcodes with classic COSMAC VIP semantics:
  00E0 CLS (clear display, drawFlag=true); 00EE RET (pc=stack.pop());
  1nnn JP addr; 2nnn CALL (stack.push(pc), pc=nnn); 3xkk SE skip if Vx==kk; 4xkk SNE skip if Vx!=kk; 5xy0 SE skip if Vx==Vy; 6xkk LD Vx=kk; 7xkk ADD Vx+=kk (no flag);
  8xy0 Vx=Vy; 8xy1 Vx|=Vy; 8xy2 Vx&=Vy; 8xy3 Vx^=Vy; 8xy4 Vx+=Vy with VF=1 if sum>255 else 0, Vx&=0xFF; 8xy5 Vx-=Vy with VF=1 if Vx>=Vy(before) else 0; 8xy6 VF=Vx&1 then Vx>>=1; 8xy7 Vx=Vy-Vx with VF=1 if Vy>=Vx(before) else 0; 8xyE VF=(Vx>>7)&1 then Vx=(Vx<<1)&0xFF;
  9xy0 SNE skip if Vx!=Vy; Annn I=nnn; Bnnn pc=nnn+V0; Cxkk Vx=(random 0..255)&kk;
  Dxyn DRW: VF=0; for row 0..n-1: byte=memory[I+row]; for bit 0..7: if byte&(0x80>>bit): px=(Vx+bit)%64, py=(Vy+row)%32, idx=py*64+px; if display[idx]==1 then VF=1; display[idx]^=1. drawFlag=true;
  Ex9E skip if keys[Vx]==1; ExA1 skip if keys[Vx]==0;
  Fx07 Vx=delayTimer; Fx0A blocking key wait: if no key pressed, pc-=2 (retry next cycle) and return; else Vx=index of pressed key; Fx15 delayTimer=Vx; Fx18 soundTimer=Vx; Fx1E I=(I+Vx)&0xFFFF; Fx29 I=0x050+(Vx&0xF)*5; Fx33 BCD: memory[I]=Math.floor(Vx/100), memory[I+1]=Math.floor(Vx/10)%10, memory[I+2]=Vx%10; Fx55 for i=0..x memory[I+i]=v[i]; Fx65 for i=0..x v[i]=memory[I+i].
  Unknown opcode: throw or console.error with hex.
- tickTimers(): if delayTimer>0 delayTimer--; if soundTimer>0 soundTimer--.

=== DEMO ROM (built-in, byte array, loaded at startup) ===
Use exactly these bytes (a program that draws a 5x5 diamond sprite and moves it with WASD = CHIP-8 keys 5/7/8/9):
[0x60,0x1C, 0x61,0x0E, 0x63,0x01, 0x00,0xE0, 0xA2,0x2E, 0xD0,0x15, 0x62,0x07, 0xE2,0x9E, 0x12,0x14, 0x80,0x35, 0x62,0x09, 0xE2,0x9E, 0x12,0x1C, 0x80,0x34, 0x62,0x05, 0xE2,0x9E, 0x12,0x24, 0x81,0x35, 0x62,0x08, 0xE2,0x9E, 0x12,0x2C, 0x81,0x34, 0x12,0x06, 0x20,0x70,0xF8,0x70,0x20]
(V0=x start 28, V1=y start 14, V3=step 1; loop at 0x206: CLS, I=0x22E sprite, DRW V0,V1,5; then for each direction key: load key code into V2, SKP V2, jump over move, apply V0/V1 +/- V3; jump back to 0x206; sprite bytes at 0x22E.)

=== DISASSEMBLER ===
function disassemble(opcode): returns human-readable string for every opcode, e.g. "CLS", "RET", "JP 0x2AA", "CALL 0x2AA", "SE V3, 0x1F", "SNE V3, 0x1F", "SE V3, V4", "LD V3, 0x1F", "ADD V3, 0x1F", "LD V3, V4", "OR V3, V4", "AND V3, V4", "XOR V3, V4", "ADD V3, V4", "SUB V3, V4", "SHR V3", "SUBN V3, V4", "SHL V3", "SNE V3, V4", "LD I, 0x2AA", "JP V0, 0x2AA", "RND V3, 0x1F", "DRW V3, V4, 5", "SKP V3", "SKNP V3", "LD V3, DT", "LD V3, K", "LD DT, V3", "LD ST, V3", "ADD I, V3", "LD F, V3", "LD B, V3", "LD [I], V3", "LD V3, [I]", fallback "DB 0x....".

=== MAIN LOOP & WIRING ===
- requestAnimationFrame loop: if running, execute `speed` cycles per frame (read from slider), then tickTimers() once per frame (60 Hz), then if drawFlag render canvas (fillRect per lit pixel, scale 10, black bg / green pixel). Always update debugger panel contents each frame (register hex values, I/PC/SP/DT/ST, stack entries, current opcode at PC: raw hex + disassembly).
- Run button: running=true (also resumes AudioContext). Pause: running=false. Step: execute exactly one cycle (works while paused; also render + update debugger). Reset: chip8.reset(), reload current ROM (the last loaded one — keep its bytes in a variable; initially the demo ROM), running=false, redraw.
- Speed slider input event updates label text.
- File input change: read file via FileReader as ArrayBuffer, store bytes as current ROM, chip8.reset(), loadRom, update status with file name and size, auto-start running.
- Keyboard: keydown/keyup listeners map keys (case-insensitive, use e.key) per the mapping above to chip8.keys[index]=1/0 and toggle a CSS "pressed" class on the corresponding keypad button. preventDefault for mapped keys. Key press AND release must both reach the emulator.
- Keypad buttons also respond to pointerdown/pointerup/pointerleave (mouse/touch) setting keys[index]=1/0 and the pressed class, so every visible control works.
- Sound: WebAudio oscillator beep (~440Hz square, low gain) playing only while soundTimer>0 and running; create AudioContext lazily on first user gesture (Run button click or keydown); resume if suspended.
- Status line updates: "RUNNING — builtin demo (51 bytes)" / "PAUSED" etc.
- On page load: chip8.reset(), load demo ROM, render once, update debugger, status shows demo loaded and PAUSED (do not auto-run).

Code must be clean, commented section headers, and complete — no placeholders, no TODOs."}
